title: Closed-fibre transfer for a directed limit over rings
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal, and f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A a morphism. Let Lambda be a nonempty directed preordered set, B a covariant diagram of commutative rings with a colimiting cocone alpha:B\to A [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], X an inverse scheme diagram with affine transitions [pqf-def-affine-morphism], g:X\to\operatorname{Spec}B a natural morphism, and p:Y\to X a limiting cone. Assume p_i;g_i=f;\operatorname{Spec}(alpha_i). There is an inverse diagram D with affine transitions and a limiting cone pi from Y times over Spec A with Spec(A/I) [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every i there is an isomorphism e_i:D_i\cong X_i times over Spec B_i with Spec(B_i/alpha_i^{-1}(I)). The first projection composed with p_i equals pi_i;e_i followed by the first stage projection, and pi_i;e_i followed by the second stage projection equals the base projection followed by Spec of the induced quotient alpha_i. There is no properness or finite-type assumption.

proof.text: Naturality sends the inverse-image ideal K_i into K_j. Define quotient transitions by Ideal.quotientMap. Every element of A/I comes from a stage; a representative whose image lies in I belongs to K_i. Compatible maps out of the quotient stages therefore induce a unique map out of A/I, giving the quotient colimit.

Apply Spec to the quotient colimit and form stagewise pullbacks of g_i. Induced transitions and cone maps satisfy the two projection equations. The universal property of each pullback, the supplied limit of X, and the Spec limits identify compatible maps to the stages with maps to the closed fibre of Y; hence the cone is limiting.

For an arrow from stage j to stage i, factor the induced fibre transition through X_j times over X_i with its closed fibre. The first arrow is a closed immersion because the extended K_i is contained in K_j. The second is a base change of the given affine transition. Both are affine, and their composite is affine. Identity isomorphisms can be used for the stage pullbacks.

lean.statement: theorem quotient_fibre_limit_transfer {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of A)) {Λ : Type u} [Preorder Λ] [Nonempty Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)] (B : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (Xs : Λᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (g : Xs ⟶ B.op ⋙ Scheme.Spec) (α : B ⟶ (Functor.const Λ).obj (.of A)) (p : (Functor.const Λᵒᵖ).obj Y ⟶ Xs) (hc : Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk _ α))) (hl : Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk _ p))) (ha : ∀ {i j : Λᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (Xs.map a)) (hw : ∀ i, p.app i ≫ g.app i = f ≫ Spec.map (α.app i.unop)) : ∃ (D : Λᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (π : (Functor.const Λᵒᵖ).obj (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))) ⟶ D), Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk _ π)) ∧ (∀ {i j : Λᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map a)) ∧ ∀ i : Λᵒᵖ, ∃ e : D.obj i ≅ pullback (g.app i) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.comap (α.app i.unop).hom)))), pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) ≫ p.app i = (π.app i ≫ e.hom) ≫ pullback.fst (g.app i) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.comap (α.app i.unop).hom)))) ∧ (π.app i ≫ e.hom) ≫ pullback.snd (g.app i) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.comap (α.app i.unop).hom)))) = pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.quotientMap I (α.app i.unop).hom le_rfl))
